title: MinION Nanopore Identification and Genomic Characterization of Pseudomonas syringae
author: Burlakoti, Sapkota, et al.
materials: Personal protective equipment (PPE), including laboratory coat, nitrile gloves, protective eyewear
Sterile Petri dishes (VWR, cat. no. CA25389‐328)

This protocol details the extraction of genomic DNA from blueberry tissues infected with Pseudomonas spp. using the Qiagen DNeasy Plant Mini Kit with some modifications in sample preparation and lysis of the plant tissue. The procedure is designed to maximize yield and purity from plant tissues that often contain high levels of polysaccharides and secondary metabolites, which can inhibit downstream applications.

steps.title: Collect and store plant samples
steps.instruction: Place symptomatic blueberry leaves, stems, or floral buds into airtight Ziploc bags, remove any visible moisture with a paper towel, and store the bags at 4 °C until processing.

substeps.instruction: Enclose plant material in an airtight bag (e.g., Ziploc).
If moisture is present, absorb it with a paper towel.

steps.title: Inspect and record sample symptoms
steps.instruction: Before processing, examine each sample with the naked eye, a magnifying lens, or a stereo microscope and record observed symptoms such as necrosis, discoloration, tissue distortion, stunting, or wilting.

steps.title: Perform all isolation inside BSC
steps.instruction: Carry out every isolation step for pseudomonad cultures inside a certified biological safety cabinet (BSC) to maintain sample integrity, ensure user safety, and prevent environmental contamination.

steps.title: Isolate pseudomonad cultures from tissue
steps.instruction: Using the stored plant material, isolate plant‑pathogenic pseudomonads by the laboratory’s standard culture methods (e.g., surface sterilization, plating on selective media) while working inside the BSC.

steps.title: Extract DNA from pure cultures
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from the isolated pure Pseudomonas cultures with the Bio‑Rad InstaGene Matrix kit, following the manufacturer’s rapid protocol to obtain PCR‑ready DNA.

steps.title: Extract DNA from infected plant tissue
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA directly from infected blueberry tissues using the Qiagen DNeasy Plant Mini Kit, applying the described modifications to sample preparation and lysis.

steps.title: Quality control and library preparation
steps.instruction: Assess DNA quality, then barcode each sample and ligate sequencing adapters using the Oxford Nanopore Native Barcoding Kit 24 V14 according to the kit instructions, multiplexing up to 24 samples per run while minimizing DNA shearing and contamination.

substeps.instruction: Perform DNA quality checks (e.g., concentration, purity).
Assign a barcode to each sample using the Native Barcoding Kit 24 V14.
Ligate sequencing adapters as instructed by the kit.
Pool up to 24 barcoded samples for multiplexed sequencing.

steps.title: Run MinION sequencing
steps.instruction: Load the prepared library onto an Oxford Nanopore MinION flow cell and execute the sequencing run according to the MinION software protocol.
